title: refactor: rename projects to a microkernel-style layout
description:
Rename the solution to reflect a microkernel (plug-in) architecture. The kernel is Timetracker.App; the shared plug-in contract and the add-ins move under a Timetracker.Plugins.* prefix.

## Decisions (locked)

- Folder layout: FLAT dotted folders (Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts/, Timetracker.Plugins.AzureDevOps/, Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor/ as siblings of Timetracker.App/).
- ActivityMonitor exe name: FULL CONSISTENCY — assembly/exe renamed to Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor, updating the ~7 hardcoded filename strings (alternative was keeping the exe name stable; rejected for cleanliness).

## Target layout

- Timetracker.App -> unchanged (exe stays Timetracker).
- Timetracker.Plugins -> Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts.
- Timetracker.AzureDevOps -> Timetracker.Plugins.AzureDevOps.
- Timetracker.ActivityMonitor -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor.
- Test projects: Timetracker.Plugins.Tests.Unit -> Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts.Tests.Unit; Timetracker.AzureDevOps.Tests.Unit -> Timetracker.Plugins.AzureDevOps.Tests.Unit; Timetracker.ActivityMonitor.Tests.Unit -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor.Tests.Unit. UI and Architecture test projects unchanged.

## Namespace mapping

- Timetracker.Plugins -> Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts
- Timetracker.Plugins.Interfaces -> Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts.Interfaces
- Timetracker.AzureDevOps(.Views) -> Timetracker.Plugins.AzureDevOps(.Views)
- Timetracker.ActivityMonitor(.Interfaces) -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor(.Interfaces)
- The three test namespaces follow their new project names.

## Change inventory

1. git mv 4 folders; update Timetracker.slnx paths.
2. csproj: RootNamespace everywhere; ActivityMonitor AssemblyName -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor; project references in App.csproj (3 paths + publish-target ActivityMonitorOutputDir/MSBuild Projects path) and both add-in csproj (-> ..\Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts\) and test csproj.
3. InternalsVisibleTo: AzureDevOps and ActivityMonitor -> new test assembly names.
4. Namespace + using changes: Timetracker.Plugins (4 files), AzureDevOps (5 + 2 Views), ActivityMonitor (~15 + 2 Interfaces), App (App.cs, HookRegistry.cs, TrackerViewModel.cs, TrackerTabView.cs, WeekTabView.cs, Components/WeekTrackingTree.cs). HookRegistry.cs bare prefixes AzureDevOps.X / ActivityMonitor.X become Plugins.AzureDevOps.X / Plugins.ActivityMonitor.X.
5. String refs: ProjectReferenceRules.cs (PluginsProject constant -> Timetracker.Plugins.Contracts; uiTest.References("Timetracker.AzureDevOps") -> new name); embedded resource "Timetracker.AzureDevOps.azure-favicon.png" -> "Timetracker.Plugins.AzureDevOps.azure-favicon.png" in loader + AzureDevOpsPanelRenderTests.cs; ActivityMonitor exe/log names in WindowsActivityMonitorInstaller, LinuxActivityMonitorInstaller, MonitorLog, App.csproj publish target, ActivityMonitor.Tests.Unit TestSupport + MonitorLogTests.
6. README: update project-structure tree and prose naming the old projects.
7. GitHub workflow release.yml: packaging step must reference the renamed monitor exe — Timetracker.ActivityMonitor -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor and Timetracker.ActivityMonitor.exe -> Timetracker.Plugins.ActivityMonitor.exe (3 occurrences in the tar/zip packaging, lines ~72-74). ci.yml needs NO change (it only publishes/uploads the App, whose project path and exe name Timetracker are unchanged).

## Validation

Single atomic change (no partial-rename build). dotnet build; dotnet test (architecture tests must still pass: reference rules + interface namespace rule); dotnet format --verify-no-changes (reapply CRLF to any rewritten LF files). Commit Conventional Commits + this issue id.

title: feat: enforce MVVM with architecture tests and separate layers
description:
Goal: enforce, with automated architecture tests, that the Timetracker app follows MVVM.

- Views -> ViewModels (among Timetracker.* namespaces; Avalonia.*/System.*/Microsoft.* are framework, always allowed)
- ViewModels -> Models (among Timetracker.* namespaces)
- ViewModels never depend on Avalonia/Avalonia.*

Two-part effort: add the architecture test, then refactor until green.

## Phase 1 - Architecture test
New file: Timetracker.Tests.Architecture/MvvmRules.cs (ArchUnitNET fluent DSL, snake_case NUnit tests, AwesomeAssertions, offender lists, guard test). Scoped to the Timetracker assembly.

1. View_models_do_not_depend_on_avalonia
2. View_models_depend_only_on_models (forbidden: Services, Interfaces, ActivityMonitor.*, Views, Plugins.*)
3. Views_depend_only_on_view_models (forbidden: Models, Services, Interfaces, Plugins.*)
4. There_are_view_models_and_views_to_check (guard)

## Phase 2 - Full MVVM separation

### 2a. Views -> only ViewModels
- EditEntriesWindow.cs: drop Timetracker.Models (TrackerEntry); expose surviving sessions via EditEntriesViewModel.
- Add-in UI contribution (WeekTabView, TrackerTabView, WeekTrackingTree): stop resolving IUiContributor/IWeekDayContributor and implementing host interfaces in Views; route status/task-name through ViewModels; build add-in Controls in a Timetracker.Services helper and inject via constructors. Touches Plugins/Interfaces Hooks/Hosts, UiHostAccessor, ActivityMonitor, AzureDevOps.

### 2b. ViewModels -> only Models
- TrackerViewModel.cs (762 lines): extract orchestration into a Timetracker.Services coordinator (repository/timer/idle/stopwatch); reduce ViewModel to state + commands fed by Func<>/Action<> delegates; remove ErrorLog from ViewModels.

### 2c. Update tests
- TrackerViewModelTests (~60 ctor sites), EditEntriesViewModelTests, TestDoubles, and Timetracker.Tests.UI.

## Validation
dotnet build, dotnet test, dotnet format --verify-no-changes. Conventional Commits + issue id.

## Notes
Large refactor crossing App, Plugins, ActivityMonitor, AzureDevOps, and test projects. Add the test first (fails), then refactor to green. Optional smaller first slice: Avalonia rule + EditEntriesWindow/ErrorLog only.

title: refactor: make tracker file I/O asynchronous
description:
Move tracker persistence off the UI thread.

Currently JsonTrackerRepository does blocking File.ReadAllText/WriteAllText/Replace on the UI thread during Start/Stop/edit/delete. Make the persistence layer async and await it from the view model.

## Changes

1. ITrackerRepository (Timetracker.App/Interfaces/ITrackerRepository.cs): rename to async methods:
   - Task<IReadOnlyList<TrackerEntry>> GetAllAsync()
   - Task AddAsync(TrackerEntry entry)
   - Task SaveAsync(IReadOnlyList<TrackerEntry> entries)

2. JsonTrackerRepository (Services/JsonTrackerRepository.cs):
   - LoadEntries() -> LoadEntriesAsync() using File.ReadAllTextAsync
   - WriteAll/WriteText -> async using File.WriteAllTextAsync
   - Keep File.Replace/Move/Copy synchronous (no async API; fast same-volume metadata ops)

3. TrackerViewModel (ViewModels/TrackerViewModel.cs): make repo-touching methods async:
   - RefreshEntries() -> RefreshEntriesAsync() (GetAllAsync)
   - Save(TrackerEntry) -> async (AddAsync)
   - DeleteEntries, ReplaceSessions, UpdateEntryText -> async Task (SaveAsync)
   - Stop()/HaltAndSave() -> async (only Stop writes; Start stays sync)
   - SaveRunningEntryOnClose() -> async

4. Command support: only the Stop command becomes async. Add a small AsyncRelayCommand in ViewModels/ (accepts Func<Task>, exposes RaiseCanExecuteChanged). No existing equivalent exists.

5. View call sites (already async-friendly):
   - EntryHistoryGrid.cs: DeleteEntries (line ~281), ReplaceSessions in OpenEditor (~234), UpdateEntryText via Dispatcher.UIThread.Post (~299)
   - EditEntriesWindow.cs: ReplaceSessions
   - TrackerWindow.cs: SaveRunningEntryOnClose (~65)

6. Tests: update ITrackerRepository fakes and calls to async in TrackerViewModelTests, JsonTrackerRepositoryTests, TrackerFileMigratorTests, EditEntriesViewModelTests, HookRegistryTests, TestDoubles, and the UI-test FakeRepo classes (WeekTreeIndentTests, ColumnResizeTests, WeekCopyButtonTests, WeekContributorPlacementTests, RowActionSortTests). FakeItEasy: ReturnsLazily -> Task.FromResult.

## Design decisions (locked)

- Initial load: constructor fires _ = RefreshEntriesAsync(); expose public RefreshEntriesAsync() tests can await. Avalonia SynchronizationContext posts continuations back to the UI thread.
- Close-save: SaveRunningEntryOnClose uses a single deliberate .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on the close path (documented as the one justified exception to no-blocking, to avoid losing the running entry on exit).

## Architecture-test implication

UnitTestStructureRules enforces test naming after the method under test. Renaming GetAll->GetAllAsync etc. requires tests named GetAll_When... to be renamed GetAllAsync_When...

title: Add git commit hook for committing
description: Add an required git commit hook. Whenever a commit is made it must have an issue id mentioned at the end.
close_reason: Implemented in 8680c3e: commit-msg now requires the subject to end with the tracked issue id (e.g. '(timetracker-66k)') in addition to Conventional Commits; merges/reverts exempt, --no-verify bypasses. .beads/hooks/commit-msg delegates to .githooks/commit-msg (single source of truth); .beads/hooks/* forced to LF in .gitattributes to fix a fresh-clone 'bad interpreter' failure. README + AGENTS.md updated.

title: Tracking View for Weekview
description:
Instead of showing the entries for the Weekview either per TrackerEntry, or grouped by booking element, we shall provide a treeview.

The weekview is redesigned, in a way, that it shows for a given day and all TrackerEntries grouped, by BookingElement, in a kind of treeview:
* (+|-) Monday yyyy-mm-dd
  * (+|-) <Booking Element> (hh:mm) [Copy Button]
    * <TrackerEntry> (hh:mm) [Copy Button]

For every weekday, there is a line with an expand (+) or collapse (-) icon. Than the next level shows the Booking Elements, with the sum of the time spent, for each TrackingEntry, for that given day. The next level shows the TrackingEntries with the total time spent on them for that given day.

The copy button of the items, shall only copy the name of the items not its time spent. The previous, current, and next week buttons remain unchaged. 

By default, all entries are collapsed when opening the view. When the week is changed, also all entries are shown collapsed.
design:
## Redesign: week view as a collapsible tree

Replace the seven side-by-side day columns with a single vertical tree:

    [-/+] Mon 21.09.   SUM 1:30        PC 7:15 active / 1:20 idle
        [-/+] Project X (1:30)  [copy]
              Report (1:00)  [copy]
              Review (0:30)  [copy]
        [-/+] <None> (1:00)  [copy]
    [-/+] Tue 22.09.
    [-/+] Wed 23.09.
    ...                                (all seven days, always present)

### Confirmed decisions

1. Day caption keeps the current "Mon 21.09." format.
2. The day row shows the day's sum (e.g. "1:30" with the sigma).
3. Every **booking element** copy button copies the **task names inside that
   element group**, one per line. This supersedes the earlier "<element>"
   copy semantics and applies to all booking-element copy buttons.
4. Entries with no booking element form their own group named "<None>".
5. Entry (leaf) rows are merged by task name, with the summed duration.
6. The "Group by booking element" checkbox is removed; the tree always groups
   Day -> Booking element -> Task.
7. All nodes start collapsed, and collapse again whenever the week changes.
   Expansion is kept across live data refreshes (a session being saved).
8. The gray PC activity line is appended to the day row.

### Architecture (view models)

- WeekViewModel (changed): drops GroupByBookingElement/SetGrouping; a week
  change collapses all nodes; UpdateSessions/UpdateActivitySpans keep the
  user's expansion. Also drops the unused ActivityText/UpdateActivitySpans
  path (dead code: the visible PC line comes from IWeekDayContributor).
- WeekDayViewModel (changed): day node with IsExpanded + ToggleCommand and
  Groups as IReadOnlyList<WeekElementGroupViewModel>; EntriesText removed.
- WeekElementGroupViewModel (new): element node with Name ("<None>" when
  empty), TotalText, IsExpanded, ToggleCommand, CopyText (task names), Entries.
- WeekEntryViewModel (new): leaf node with Task, TotalText, CopyText.
- WeekDayGroup (removed): superseded by the node view models.

Ordering: elements then tasks by earliest start, tie-broken by name. Grouping
and matching are case-insensitive (first-seen spelling kept), consistent with
the history list.

Expansion lifecycle:

    Move(+/-7) / MoveToCurrentWeek() -> Rebuild() -> collapse all
    UpdateSessions(...)              -> Rebuild() -> keep day IsExpanded,
                                                     match element IsExpanded by name

### Architecture (view)

WeekDaysGrid is replaced by Views/Components/WeekTrackingTree.cs, built the
same imperative way (no XAML), taking the IWeekDayContributor list (day-row
activity) and an IWeekStatusHost (copy feedback). WeekTabView drops the
checkbox; the prev/current/next toolbar, title, week total, contributor band
and status line stay unchanged.

### Plan slices

1. View models + unit tests (tree model, "<None>", expansion lifecycle).
2. WeekTrackingTree + WeekTabView cutover (checkbox removed).
3. UI tests + README updated; full validation (build, test, format, TZ=UTC).
close_reason: Implemented in cfbf0e0: week view is now a collapsible day/element/task tree; all nodes collapse on open and on week change, expansion survives live refreshes; <None> group for entries without a booking element; element/task copy buttons copy names only; day sum and PC activity on the day node; checkbox and dead ActivityText path removed. 180 tests pass.

title: refactor: remove the empty AzureDevOpsService.Dispose
description:
Timetracker.AzureDevOps/AzureDevOpsService.cs declares IDisposable (line 11) with an empty Dispose() (lines 98-100). The service owns nothing to dispose: the AzureDevOpsClient is created per call via _clientFactory and disposed in the using inside ApplyIssueAsync.

Changes:
- Drop IDisposable from the class declaration
- Delete the empty Dispose() method

AzureDevOpsClient keeps its own IDisposable (it disposes the HttpClient). No other call sites dispose the service (verified by grep); removing IDisposable stops the DI container from invoking the no-op on shutdown.

title: docs: correct the RelayCommand summary
description:
The RelayCommand XML doc summary (Timetracker.App/ViewModels/RelayCommand.cs lines 5-8) says 'for WinForms, where no CommandManager exists'. This app is Avalonia, not WinForms — the comment is stale (copied from elsewhere).

Replace the summary with an accurate description, e.g. 'Basic ICommand implementation; the view model calls RaiseCanExecuteChanged when CanExecute might have changed.'

One-line documentation edit, no behavior change.
